correctness.rationale: Proof splits all possible hub actions. With same hubs positive page weights force every page opposite, and hub flips compare A,B with tau. With opposite hubs, each a_i>b_i page must oppose u, each a_i<b_i opposes v, ties freely choose S; hub deviations impose 2(A_L+w(S))>=A-tau and 2(B_L+w(S))<=B+tau. This bijects Nash profiles with two complements for each valid subset and two aligned cuts when stable. Each cut total equals X=A+B or Y=tau+sum max(a_i,b_i), social welfare twice cut; maximum cut is stable because unilateral payoff change equals cut change. Split threshold follows by minimizing both inequality bounds over S. For even k the tie count is binom(k,k/2); the proposed epsilon perturbation leaves two optimal aligned profiles because v would flip in the only opposite-hub candidate. Independent rational brute-force enumerated 240 positive rational settings, 6912 labeled profiles (k=2,3), matching counts, welfare and PoA; no finite enumeration is used for all real weights.
